runners_data.name: Deputy Vice
runners_data.comment: Third on debut last month and then disappointing at Carlisle last time, Deputy Vice has the course and distance experience on good going and should be capable of improvement once that below-par effort is set aside; the trainer’s recent form is a concern, but the ability shown on debut suggests he remains a threat.

runners_data.name: Dreamlover
runners_data.comment: A promising 3½-length fourth on debut at Southwell, Dreamlover has had time to progress since that first outing and now adds blinkers for a trainer in good form; sprint-bred, he is entitled to do better with experience and his market position bears watching.

runners_data.name: Stardom Glory
runners_data.comment: Placed on both starts to date including second at York last time beaten 2 lengths, Stardom Glory has been consistent over this trip on good going and tops our figures; he is yet to go one better but his form has been solid and he looks the clear pick here.

runners_data.name: The Dancing Pirate
runners_data.comment: Fourth beaten just 1½ lengths in a 2-year-old race at Beverley last time, The Dancing Pirate was far from disgraced and fast ground suits his action; a top course trainer gives him every chance and he should improve further, making him a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Walt
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on his only start at Haydock, Walt showed little on debut and sits at the foot of our figures here; cheekpieces are added and he could do better if settled off the pace, but a significant step forward from that first run is needed to threaten.

runners_data.name: Trust Havana
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in two starts to date including here last time, Trust Havana has yet to show much ability; her breeding suggests speed and a third run could bring some improvement, though she needs considerable progress to threaten in this company.

runners_data.name: Eagle Bay
runners_data.comment: Landed his maiden by 5 lengths at Thirsk last time out after a promising debut, building steadily on that earlier effort; effective at 7f on good ground and looks to have more in the locker, giving him every chance in this small field.

runners_data.name: Albemagic
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a novice on his only start, so there is plenty to prove here; if he can settle better at the start and race more positively he holds some potential, but a significant step up is needed on debut form.

runners_data.name: El Nay
runners_data.comment: Consistent in the places and beaten only a short-head last time, showing form close to his best; effective at 7f on today's going and holds a fair chance, though he remains yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Remi Mae
runners_data.comment: Returned a poor handicap debut 162 days ago when overraced and out of her depth in open company; she handles today's trip and going and is trained by one of this venue's most successful handlers, but she has something to prove after that run.

races.name: Manor Car Hire Handicap

runners_data.name: Stratusnine
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Hugo Palmer with David Egan aboard; holds five similar-going runs and has been placed at 6f on Good, making this a track-appropriate assignment — though classified as a prominent-style runner officially, this horse is effectively the race's pace-setter and its chance hinges entirely on how long it can sustain the lead.|
runners_data.comment: Tried over a longer trip last time and beaten 5 lengths; back to his preferred 6f now and acts on this going, but an inconsistent recent sequence — including a pull-up and unseating — makes him hard to trust, and the wide draw is another factor.

runners_data.name: Dark Thirty
runners_data.note: Jason Hart partners this experienced six-year-old who won over this exact C&D trip on Good ground, boasting three wins and five places from ten similar-going starts; a pure hold-up operator who needs the pace to be genuine and room to emerge late in Chester's cramped straight.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time at this same mark, he handles 6f on any ground and enjoys making the running; our figures rate him clear of these, though he has yet to land from a mark this high and his trainer is currently short of winners.

runners_data.name: Solar Aclaim
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides for Julie Camacho, but the form string of 0-0081 raises concern — this horse's best recent form came on Soft ground and its two similar-going runs produced no wins or places; the step up in class and drop back from soft ground is a notable negative.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a 2.25-length handicap success last time off a mark 8lb lower than today's, so a significant rise has to be navigated; effective at this trip but prefers cut in the ground, and the good conditions here may blunt his effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Stormy Impact
runners_data.note: Ethan Tindall claims 5lb on this Richard Fahey four-year-old who has placed twice at 6f, most recently on Softer ground; races prominently but has only nine similar-going runs and the apprentice claim may help offset a modest recent record — 21 days since last run is manageable.|
runners_data.comment: Ran marginally closer to form last time when beaten 2.25 lengths off this mark; usually held up and acts on a sound surface — both relevant here — though a bounce back is needed on overall recent results and the wide draw is an added factor.

runners_data.name: We Never Stop
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves partners this Kevin Ryan five-year-old wearing a hood; the form string 793800 reads poorly and the horse has failed to win in six similar-going starts — drawn in a field likely to see little pace, this hold-up horse faces a tough ask in Chester's short straight with modest recent form.|
runners_data.comment: Down the field in recent starts and yet to score in his last six runs; handles today's trip and going but appears far more effective on the all-weather, and first-time cheekpieces face a stiff task against these rivals.

runners_data.name: Purest Time
runners_data.note: Ian Williams sends out this six-year-old 47 days fresh, and Edward Greatrex takes the ride; a genuine hold-up horse by nature who has been mapped to midfield because the field carries more prominent types than can secure position — its best recent win came at 6f on Good, but racing further forward than natural will be a challenge.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap last time with something to spare, asserting through the final furlong; the new mark is considered manageable and he handles today's trip and conditions, though his record either side of that success has been patchy.

runners_data.name: Rosenpur
runners_data.note: George Wood rides for Jennie Candlish, and this horse arrives wearing a hood on a 14-day turnaround; has won at 6f on Good ground and carries eleven similar-going starts showing three wins and seven places — an honest prominent type who could genuinely secure a front-rank berth and is one of the most track-appropriate profiles in the field.|
runners_data.comment: A three-time winner at this venue, he scored over course and distance two starts back off a 4lb lower mark; he enjoys front-running on good ground and wears a first-time hood, though last time was a touch below that level at the same mark.

runners_data.name: Candonomore
runners_data.note: Sean Levey partners Jennie Candlish's five-year-old who wears a tongue-tie and cheekpieces; naturally races prominently but this field has compressed that position — Candonomore's recent form string 522136 shows consistency, though its five sim-going runs at 7-9f suggest the six-furlong trip here may be sharp and the style mismatch is a real concern.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a 3-length success three starts back before form dipped away; the same mark here asks more than he's shown of late, though first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces could help his cause.

runners_data.name: Ruby's Angel
runners_data.note: David Probert rides this Hugo Palmer three-year-old who won over 6f on Good ground and has an excellent 2W5P record from nine similar-going starts; a prominent type with strong recent form who is well-placed to secure a handy position and benefits from carrying the lightest weight in the field at 126lbs.|
runners_data.comment: A past course-and-distance winner who landed a neck success here two starts back; last time was well below that — 16th and beaten 9 lengths off this same mark — so a significant bounce back is needed, though the C&D record is a genuine positive.

races.paceDynamic: Stratusnine is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to dictate from the front at a sustainable, uncontested gallop around Chester's tight circuit. Stormy Impact and Ruby's Angel will press forward into prominent positions, but neither is a natural front-runner, meaning the pace Stratusnine sets is unlikely to be truly pressured or excessive. This field carries a surplus of prominent types — Candonomore and Purest Time are genuine pace-seeking horses whose natural positions have been squeezed out; Rosenpur and Ruby's Angel are better placed to actually secure front-rank berths, while Candonomore and Purest Time will need to settle for a lower position than ideal. A controlled, single-pace gallop on Good ground at Chester over 6f strongly favours horses who can race prominently and travel smoothly through the race, with true hold-up types left with insufficient room and run in the straight to make up ground from rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stratusnine Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Stratusnine is allowed to stride clear at a steady tempo and the field fails to apply sustained pressure.
scenarios.body: If Stratusnine is allowed to stride clear at a steady tempo and the field fails to apply sustained pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Ruby's Angel or Stormy Impact press the pace hard enough to weaken Stratusnine before the straight.
scenarios.body: If Ruby's Angel or Stormy Impact press the pace hard enough to weaken Stratusnine before the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that the rear of the field can close the gap through tired rivals in the straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that the rear of the field can close the gap through tired rivals in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses battle for position early, causing a ragged tempo and leaving the race open late.
scenarios.body: If multiple prominent horses battle for position early, causing a ragged tempo and leaving the race open late.

watchPoints.text: Stratusnine sets the pace entirely alone — if David Egan is allowed a completely uncontested lead at a crawl, no closer will be able to bridge the gap in Chester's tight home straight.

Candonomore and Purest Time are naturally prominent/prominent-hold-up types who cannot get their preferred position in this race shape — watch for both to be shuffled back early, which would significantly reduce their winning chances.

Ruby's Angel carries just 126lbs and has two wins from nine Good-ground starts — if she travels smoothly just off Stratusnine's shoulder, her light weight and proven form make her a live danger from the prominent group in the straight.

Rosenpur's hood fitting and 14-day turnaround for Jennie Candlish is worth noting — the trainer has 2/23 in the 14-day window, but this horse's C&D form on Good ground gives it the most relevant profile of any hold-up-adjacent runner in the field.

Solar Aclaim's only recent win came on Soft ground and its two Good-ground runs produced no place — Good going here is a legitimate concern and Joanna Mason's 4/26 trainer strike rate in the period adds no particular confidence.

races.name: Queen Charlotte Fillies' Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Circe
runners_data.note: Ran well fresh at Goodwood last time (7f, Good, won), handles this trip and going well; Sean Levey is an accomplished handler of Chester's tight turns and she races prominently, ideally positioned to be on Copacabana Sands' quarters throughout.
runners_data.comment: Won a Listed contest at Musselburgh last time by a length and a quarter, the return to seven furlongs working well on her seasonal comeback — she acts on any going and is effective at today's trip, rating as a serious threat to our selection.

runners_data.name: Beaujolais Nouveau
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly whose recent win came over 6f on Good ground; headgear noted (p), and at 15 days since last run is fresh enough — her hold-up style means she needs genuine pace and a clean run, and Chester's short straight is a genuine concern for her profile.
runners_data.comment: Below her best when fifth at York last time, though the step up to today's trip should suit and first-time cheekpieces may help — she handles this going, but there is plenty to prove at this level.

runners_data.name: Bellarchi
runners_data.note: Hat-trick possible after back-to-back 7f wins on Good and Soft; Grant Tuer's yard is in form (T14: 1/15) and Joanna Mason will look to park her prominently on the inside rail — this trip and surface suits, and 37 days since last run is not a worry given her recent consistency.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Musselburgh by four and a quarter lengths last time in a taking effort, and coming back to this course suits — she handles today's trip and going well and looks progressive, though a 37-day absence is the main question.

runners_data.name: Brazilian Rose
runners_data.note: Genuinely prominent in style but the congestion of front-runners in this field means she is likely to find herself racing further back than ideal; her one run on Good ground showed limited ability in this grade, and the style mismatch compounds the concern.
runners_data.comment: Acquitted herself well when beaten three and a half lengths in Listed company last time, though that step up in class may have overstated her level — our figures rank her last in the field, and her trainer is in very poor current form.

runners_data.name: Copacabana Sands
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner with course-winning form over 7f on Good; Andrew Balding's yard is in solid form and Jason Watson will take her straight to the front — 49 days since last run is a mild flag, and the STYLE_FIT tag is a reminder she may not get a pure lead if rivals decide to commit, though that looks unlikely given the field map.
runners_data.comment: Eased beaten seven lengths in a Group 3 at Lingfield last time, seemingly discomforted by the fast conditions after a long break — today's ground may be more amenable, and her trainer carries a strong record at this course, but she has something to prove.

runners_data.name: Dash Of Azure
runners_data.note: Won over this trip and going at Haydock but has beaten only one home in two subsequent starts, including a poor effort 10 days ago; her natural prominent style cannot be reproduced in this crowded field, and recent form makes her hard to trust regardless of pace.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a Group 2 at Ascot on her most recent start, where the level looked beyond her at this stage of the season — our figures nonetheless rate her among the leading contenders and today's trip and going suit.

runners_data.name: La Brodeuse
runners_data.note: Improved to finish second at Newmarket over 7f on Good last time, her best effort for Kevin Ryan; a genuine front-to-prominent type who will find herself racing further back than she would like — if she can settle and pick up from a midfield position, her form entitles her to a place at least, but her best comes when on the front foot.
runners_data.comment: A consistent performer at Listed level, she ran a committed front-running race when fourth beaten two lengths in a Listed event at Musselburgh last time — she acts on any going and rates a solid threat, though her trainer's recent form is the main cloud.

runners_data.name: Magic Basma
runners_data.note: Two placed efforts from five starts at 7f suggest the trip suits; Tom Eaves will look to race her prominently for Kevin Ryan, and her consistency in good company (two seconds at 7f) makes her a solid each-way candidate if she gets a clean run behind the pace-setter.
runners_data.comment: Ran second in a Listed event at Musselburgh last time over today's trip, doing so without the clearest of passages — she acts on any going and handles seven furlongs well, and our figures rate her at the top of this field, giving her every chance.

runners_data.name: Royalty Bay
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip and going at Wolverhampton last time and is held up by Dale Swift for Seb Spencer; the small yard (T14: 0/7) is a concern in Listed company, but her late-running style is best served if the pace is genuine — she needs everything to go right on a track that doesn't flatter closers.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Musselburgh last time by a short-head in a clear step up from her seasonal debut — acts on any going, and the trip suits, but this is a sizeable class rise and the opposition is formidable.

runners_data.name: Temperance
runners_data.note: Listed as a NON-RUNNER; 352 days off the track and has not run since being pulled up — no assessment possible as she will not take part.

runners_data.name: Forty Years On
runners_data.note: Five wins from eight career starts including four at 7f, and clearly progressive, but also a NON-RUNNER here; her natural front-running style would have been squeezed out in this field anyway, and the redistribution to midfield underlines that she would have faced a positional battle had she run.

races.paceDynamic: Copacabana Sands is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to push her, she should dictate a measured, sustainable gallop around Chester's tight 7f circuit — a track where controlling the tempo from the front is a significant advantage. Behind her, Circe and Bellarchi are natural prominent types well placed to track the leader, while Magic Basma will also aim to race close to the pace. This field carries far more prominent-leaning horses than the race shape can accommodate: La Brodeuse, Dash Of Azure, Brazilian Rose, and Forty Years On are all natural front-to-prominent types that have been redistributed to midfield on the map because they simply cannot all secure their preferred position — of these, Circe and Bellarchi, racing on the rail at Chester, are most likely to actually hold prominent ground. The tactical verdict is clear: this unsustainable contest for prominent slots, combined with a lone front-runner setting a controlled pace on a track that heavily rewards horses who travel well into the bridle near the lead, strongly favours prominent-to-tracking types who can settle just off Copacabana Sands and strike decisively in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Copacabana Controls, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Copacabana Sands dictates an uncontested, measured pace and prominent types settle cleanly behind her.
scenarios.body: If Copacabana Sands dictates an uncontested, measured pace and prominent types settle cleanly behind her.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Overcrowding Causes Trouble
scenarios.trigger: If the scramble among redistributed prominent types for early position causes interference or a ragged gallop.
scenarios.body: If the scramble among redistributed prominent types for early position causes interference or a ragged gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens early enough to ensure a genuinely fast gallop and the prominent types are found out in the straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace quickens early enough to ensure a genuinely fast gallop and the prominent types are found out in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Copacabana Sands is so entirely unchallenged that she simply idles into the straight and sprints clear before rivals can respond.
scenarios.body: If Copacabana Sands is so entirely unchallenged that she simply idles into the straight and sprints clear before rivals can respond.

watchPoints.text: Copacabana Sands goes unchallenged to the front — if she rolls along uncontested, rivals tracking her (Circe, Bellarchi) must commit early enough to have cover on the rail, or risk being shut out when the gaps close in the straight.

La Brodeuse, Dash Of Azure, and Brazilian Rose may all attempt to push forward from their mapped midfield positions in the early stages, creating a bustling, fractious period between the start and the first bend that could unsettle more settled prominent types.

Royalty Bay and Beaujolais Nouveau are genuine hold-up horses dependent on a true gallop — if Copacabana Sands idles in front and the pace is dawdling, both are likely to find the 7f Chester straight too short to close from their natural positions.

Bellarchi arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and is handled by a small yard punching above its weight in Listed company — watch to see whether Joanna Mason secures rail position behind Copacabana Sands at the start, as that is the key tactical moment for her chance.

Two non-runners (Temperance, Forty Years On) reduce the field to nine effective runners, meaning the pace dynamic is slightly less pressured than the original 11-runner map suggests — this further entrenches the advantage for Copacabana Sands and the horses tracking her.

races.name: Katie O'Brien's Irish Taverns Handicap

runners_data.name: Sovereign Ocean
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who sets up this entire race; Good going suits (3 from 4 on similar ground), Marco Botti 2-from-13 over 14 days is modest but this filly's tactical position is everything — she leads and controls, but her STYLE_FIT flag notes she is technically mapped at a slight stretch and a hold on form (form string shows a 6 latest) tempers confidence she delivers.
runners_data.comment: Beaten four and a quarter lengths at Sandown last time, yet acts well at today's trip and on this surface, and he is a colt with scope to improve. That recent below-par effort is the one question.

runners_data.name: Do Bronxs
runners_data.note: David Egan takes over on this genuine hold-up horse whose best recent result was a close second over 8f on Soft; the drop back to 7f on Good is a query given six of seven similar-going runs produced no win, and this horse needs pace ahead of it that may not fully materialise.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a length and a half at this course last time off today's mark, improving on a solid earlier effort here — Chester clearly suits and our figures rate him highest in the field, though he is yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Daydreama
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby has 7 runners from 92 in 14 days — a busy yard — and Fentiman rides a horse who placed second over this exact trip on Good going; the 0 and 9 in recent form are concern but the 2/7f/GOO sits nicely in the profile if she settles close enough to pace.
runners_data.comment: Beaten seven lengths at York last time in a run consistent with his recent level — a bounce back is needed, and our figures have him well below most rivals here. He has course and going experience in his favour but is hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: First Time
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey's 3-year-old has solid placed form over 6f-7f on Good and has won at the trip; Ethan Tindall (5lb claimer) assists the weight, though 6 latest run on Good is the blot — needs to show that was a blip rather than a trend.
runners_data.comment: Ran to his level when beaten three and a quarter lengths at York last time, and he should sharpen up on that seasonal return — the stable has a strong record in this race, and today's trip and surface suit.

runners_data.name: Astrazar
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's colt won over this exact 7f trip on Good and again over 8f at Heathfield; 28 days since last run is the longest absence in the field and the 7 and 9 in latest two runs on Good are worrying, but the profile on 7f Good suggests residual ability if freshened up.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on both outings this season, with his most recent run at Carlisle leaving plenty to answer — he is yet to find his best form this year, though he acts on any going and has the ability to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Cool Molly
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner with two wins over 7f on Standard (AW), Ollie Sangster's filly is honest but the 6 and 15 in recent Good-ground form highlight a significant concern on turf — pushed to midfield here because the pace queue is full, which compounds her chance on a surface where she has yet to convince.
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye on her turf debut here in May, but her most recent run fell well short of that standard and a recovery run is needed. She has been most effective on the all-weather, with today's turf surface a sterner test.

runners_data.name: Bright Summer
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's filly won on Standard (AW) over 7f and placed over the same trip on Good; only three career runs makes her lightly raced and potentially unexposed, but her true prominent style cannot be fully expressed in this field, and she remains 0-from-1 on Good turf which is a mild flag.
runners_data.comment: Beaten ten lengths at Salisbury last time in a marked dip from her earlier success — she is effective at today's trip and going, her debut form has been franked, and her trainer has a strong record at this track.

runners_data.name: Start Me Up
runners_data.note: Ran in headgear (hg:p) last time and won over 6f on Soft most recently; Richard Spencer's gelding is a genuine hold-up horse who needs a strongly run race to get home, and 15 days since last run is fine — the concern is whether Chester's 7f on Good with a controlled front-runner produces enough pace for a finisher to close.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap here last time by three-quarters of a length, confirming his liking for Chester, and he returns in first-time cheekpieces with a trainer in form — the rise in the weights is the main query.

runners_data.name: The Resdev Scholar
runners_data.note: Consistent placer (2-4-3-3) whose true prominent style is squeezed out by the field composition; Joanna Mason rides, and the horse has placed four times in five runs on Good at 7f-8f — the form figures suggest reliability but not a winning edge, and racing out of preferred position blunts that consistency.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a length and a half at this course last time off the same mark, showing consistent form and clear course aptitude — he handles today's going and trip well, though he is yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Vidmiyr
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner for this analysis — Jennie Candlish's colt has strong placed form including a win over 7f on Good and seconds at 7f and 8f, but with no jockey declared it cannot be properly assessed; the redistribution note stands as the field had too many prominent types regardless.

races.paceDynamic: Sovereign Ocean is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to pressure her from the outset, she is likely to dictate a controlled, honest gallop around Chester's tight, flat circuit over 7f. The field, however, is packed with natural prominent-types — Cool Molly, Bright Summer, The Resdev Scholar, and Vidmiyr are all true up-with-the-pace horses who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rail positions and race shape cannot accommodate them all. Those horses will be fighting for ground early, creating a more compressed, contested early order than the lone front-runner tag implies; the pace is unlikely to be truly soft, but it should remain controlled enough that Sovereign Ocean avoids being burned off. This race shape — a single-file, honest tempo on a turning track with a bunch of natural prominent types unable to fully express themselves — favours horses who can race in the first three or four and sustain their gallop, rather than closers hoping for a messy collapse up front that is unlikely to materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sovereign Ocean Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Sovereign Ocean secures the lead without contest and sets a measured, rail-hugging tempo that stretches the field without burning herself out.
scenarios.body: If Sovereign Ocean secures the lead without contest and sets a measured, rail-hugging tempo that stretches the field without burning herself out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Grinds It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of promoted prominent types — particularly Daydreama, Astrazar and First Time — sit close to Sovereign Ocean and the race is run at a true, honest clip that suits consistent gallopers.
scenarios.body: If the cluster of promoted prominent types — particularly Daydreama, Astrazar and First Time — sit close to Sovereign Ocean and the race is run at a true, honest clip that suits consistent gallopers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Finishers Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent types crowd each other early, burning pace and creating a genuinely fast early fractions that leave the front rank vulnerable inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the prominent types crowd each other early, burning pace and creating a genuinely fast early fractions that leave the front rank vulnerable inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded prominent ranks cause significant interference early, unsettling the pace and producing an untidy race where positional disadvantage scrambles the expected order.
scenarios.body: If the crowded prominent ranks cause significant interference early, unsettling the pace and producing an untidy race where positional disadvantage scrambles the expected order.

watchPoints.text: Watch Sovereign Ocean's early position: if any of the redistributed prominent types — Cool Molly or Bright Summer — push hard for the rail exiting the stalls, Sovereign Ocean could face unexpected pressure and the entire pace scenario unravels.

Do Bronxs and Start Me Up are the only genuine hold-up horses; if the pace is moderate rather than strong, both could find themselves with no gap to close into and may finish flat despite their natural style suiting a true-run race.

Astrazar's 28-day absence is the longest in the field on a day where most rivals are 14-15 days fresh — watch the market moves for any sign the Ed Walker team expects a forward showing, as the form pre-break was deteriorating sharply.

Chester's tight turns put a premium on early position — The Resdev Scholar, Cool Molly and Bright Summer will all need to navigate around horses from wider draws; traffic risk is elevated for any horse failing to find a clear passage before the final bend.

Tim Easterby's Daydreama has a positive 7f Good profile but the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 7/92 is modest; if Fentiman is not aggressive early to sit second or third, this horse risks being swallowed by the pack of promoted prominent types.

races.name: Castillo De Ibiza EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Likealot
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner likely to lead unchallenged; Ralph Beckett handler in good recent form, though 207 days off the track is a notable query and similar-going record at this trip (1W from 9) warrants some caution — likely to control but may not find an extra gear under pressure.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap by 4 lengths last time to get back on track, though that run was 207 days ago and the ground here could work against her; first-time cheekpieces applied, but she sits bottom of our ratings against these rivals.

runners_data.name: Ciara Pearl
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves takes the ride for Kubler yard after 231 days off; best form over 10f, stepping up in trip here with a genuine hold-up style, and the good ground suits — needs a strong gallop to be produced late but Chester's short straight makes that task difficult.
runners_data.comment: First run in 231 days brings her back from a Listed race where the going may not have helped; in solid form before that and our figures rate her second-highest here, though she's yet to score in recent starts and improvement will be needed.

runners_data.name: Model Yuko
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old brings strong course-related prominent style and Roger Varian's trainer strike rate of 9/41 over 14 days shows good form; likely to track Likealot closely and the step up to 1m2½f on good ground represents her optimum conditions based on a 10f win at Goodwood last time.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a French Listed contest when last seen 296 days ago, though she ran close to her best; had been in decent shape before that and handles today's trip, but the long layoff must be overcome, despite a trainer in good form.

runners_data.name: Patagonia Girl
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's mare has genuine 3W6P form on similar going and won over 1m2f at Goodwood on her penultimate start, showing the trip suits — yet with multiple prominent types in this field she is likely to find herself shuffled back from her natural forward position, blunting that course-and-distance profile.
runners_data.comment: Last year's winner here and successful again at this course two starts back, though last time she over-raced from the front and paid the price; back in handicap company now, this trip and conditions suit and there's more to come.

runners_data.name: City Queen
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's three-year-old arrives on a 14-day turnaround having won and been placed on good and standard going repeatedly; Toby Moore's claim is a factor to weigh, but she is versatile in style, will travel close to the pace, and the step up from 1m to 1m2½f is the key question here.
runners_data.comment: Won a handicap by a head last time and has built a progressive profile with two wins in her last five starts; she handles this going, but today's 10f is a step beyond her proven range, which adds some uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Winged One
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's filly is a genuine hold-up type whose best run (2nd at 1m2f on soft) came with cover — recent form over 1m2f on good ground is mixed and she needs a strong pace to arrive from off it at Chester, where the geometry penalises late runners.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up here last time in an improved display, and the trainer has a strong record at this course; first-time cheekpieces are fitted, she handles the trip and going, and our figures rate her comfortably clear at the head of the field.

runners_data.name: Hoseki
runners_data.note: William Haggas's lightly-raced three-year-old won nicely at 1m2f on good ground last time and has class on her side, but as a naturally forward-going type she will be unable to secure that position in this field and is effectively racing against her instincts — the short racing history also means there is uncertainty about handling Chester's sharp track.
runners_data.comment: Landed her maiden by 3/4 length last time, showing improved form, and is bred for distances like today's; lightly raced, she enters handicaps with the prospect of further progress to come.

runners_data.name: Bearin Up
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's filly has been busy (10 days since last run) and boasts a solid 3W6P record on good ground — an adaptable sort at heart, but her natural inclination to race prominently is squeezed out in this field, and the 1m2½f trip at Chester represents a step into the unknown for a horse who has not raced beyond 1m1f.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap by a neck last time to return to form, and has been generally consistent; the step up to 10f is the question given she's best over 8-9f, and our figures leave her needing to outperform her position here.

races.paceDynamic: Likealot is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should settle comfortably in front at a sustainable gallop around Chester's tight, turning track over 1m2½f — a configuration that heavily rewards horses able to dictate and control tempo from the front. Model Yuko and City Queen are natural prominent racers who will likely track Likealot closely in second and third, keeping the pace honest without blowing the race apart. The field carries more prominent-minded runners than the race shape can absorb: Patagonia Girl, Hoseki, and Bearin Up are all true front-to-midfield types but are redistributed into midfield on this map, meaning they will likely be squeezed back from their natural positions, reducing their effectiveness and limiting their ability to mount a sustained challenge. This race shape — a controlled, uncontested lead at a fair but not brutal gallop — strongly favours prominent and close-tracking horses that can settle just off the pace and be delivered with a clean run on the inside at Chester, rather than genuine hold-up runners who will face traffic and distance to make up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Likealot Controls, Tracking Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Likealot leads at a measured pace and the prominent trackers get an unimpeded passage to deliver their challenge turning for home.
scenarios.body: If Likealot leads at a measured pace and the prominent trackers get an unimpeded passage to deliver their challenge turning for home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Likealot Dominates Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady and Likealot builds an unassailable lead turning in, never coming off the bridle.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely steady and Likealot builds an unassailable lead turning in, never coming off the bridle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Deliver from Deep
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply enough in the middle stages to gut the leaders and open the race up for hold-up types.
scenarios.body: If the pace quickens sharply enough in the middle stages to gut the leaders and open the race up for hold-up types.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Chaos, Prominent Types Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple redistributed prominent runners push forward early, creating an uncharacteristically contested pace scenario.
scenarios.body: If multiple redistributed prominent runners push forward early, creating an uncharacteristically contested pace scenario.

watchPoints.text: Likealot's 207-day absence is the single biggest risk to Scenario A — monitor whether she fires on reappearance or loses her early sharpness, as any hesitation from the front could unravel the dominant race shape.

City Queen's jockey booking — Toby Moore's 7lb claim — is a notable wildcard at a tight, tactical track like Chester where positional decisions are critical; watch for whether she is given a clean passage close to Likealot in the early stages.

Patagonia Girl, Hoseki, and Bearin Up could all attempt to push forward at the start despite being mapped to midfield — if two or more of these horses contest for prominent positions, watch for an uncharacteristic mid-race surge in pace that could compromise Likealot's controlled lead.

Model Yuko arrives after 296 days off and is stepping back up in trip — her prep work and paddock demeanour are worth noting, as a big absence at a track as demanding as Chester can catch out horses who are not fully wound up.

Winged One has headgear noted and was pulled up on her penultimate start before finishing second most recently — a hold-up runner at Chester where the straight is short; watch whether Jason Watson elects to be more positive than usual given the shape of this race.

races.name: Roxy Ball Room Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Venezuelan
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race, sporting a visor and returning after 28 days; P-style maps perfectly to Chester's tight circuit and uncontested lead is its greatest asset, though trainer Gary Hanmer's 14-day record of 0/12 is a mild caution.
runners_data.comment: Previously showing good form at this sort of level, Venezuelan carries course and distance experience on a sound surface and now tries a first-time visor; the worry is a below-par effort here last time and the sense that he can be a little reluctant to give his best.

runners_data.name: Midnight Rumble
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse most effective on Soft or Standard ground rather than Good, with zero wins from 15 runs on similar going — Sean Levey's booking is the main positive but the ground and Chester's track configuration both work against a late finisher.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 6½ lengths here last time, Midnight Rumble remains competitive at this level — our figures rate him second in the field — though this 16f is a real test of stamina; without a win in recent starts, the concern is that he keeps finding one or two too good.

runners_data.name: Solar Pass
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's operation is in strong form at 12/57 over 14 days and this horse has been placed on Good ground multiple times at 2m, making it the most consistent threat if it can slot in just off the pace and pick up when Venezuelan tires.
runners_data.comment: Placed three times in a row at this distance, Solar Pass has been consistently near the front and now wears first-time cheekpieces for a top course handler on a sound surface; her habit of coming up just short when it matters is the concern.

runners_data.name: Shipshape
runners_data.note: Four wins in recent form including back-to-back victories, and a P-style that suits sitting prominently on Chester's bowl — David Probert knows the track well and the hg:p headgear tag suggests it has been aided by equipment; the form line reads as the most in-form horse in the field.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last six starts include a success here last time off a 4lb lower mark, and Shipshape has been admirably consistent; first-time cheekpieces are added, but our speed figure lags well behind the principals and he faces a stiffer task at this higher mark.

runners_data.name: Curran
runners_data.note: Won its last race over 14f on Good going and boasts the most wins in similar-going conditions of any runner, but Tom Eaves inherits a H-style horse on a track where making ground from the rear is structurally very difficult at 2m.
runners_data.comment: Landing a handicap by a head at Bath last time off a 2lb lower mark, Curran showed a marked upturn in form and tops our figures; he handles the course, distance and going well and his trainer is in good shape — he is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Ruler Legend
runners_data.note: Holds strong stamina credentials — winning form over 16f and 18f on Good — and has genuine class, but 247 days off the track (with a hood noted) combined with being a true hold-up horse unable to find its natural rear position makes this a speculative angle rather than a live one.
runners_data.comment: Third beaten 3½ lengths off a mark 24lb higher over hurdles last time, Ruler Legend returns to the flat on a considerably more lenient ticket here; he landed one over the obstacles three starts back, but this is his first flat run since October and the switch back adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Furhaan
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up type whose recent Good-ground form over shorter trips (11-12f) is mostly poor, and having been redistributed to midfield from its true rear position, it lacks both the form and the positional security to figure here; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is the sole mitigation.
runners_data.comment: Below his best when beaten 4½ lengths at Hamilton last time, Furhaan has shown little in recent runs and sits at the foot of our figures; he handles good going, but this step up to 16f is unproven and he needs clear improvement to feature after 41 days off.

races.paceDynamic: Venezuelan is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no natural pace rival likely to press hard from the front, shapes to control this 2m Chester contest at a sustainable gallop from the outset. Solar Pass and Shipshape are both prominent-style horses who will attempt to track closely, meaning the early order resolves fairly cleanly around Venezuelan at the head of affairs followed by those two. Ruler Legend and Furhaan are genuine hold-up horses who cannot all find their preferred rear position given the number of hold-up types in the field — those two are mapped to midfield, but Venezuelan, Solar Pass, and Shipshape are most likely to actually secure the forward positions. A steady-to-moderate early tempo set by one uncontested front-runner over Chester's tight, turning 2m trip strongly favours horses who can race prominently and travel into the race, rather than those forced to make up ground late on a course where passing is notoriously difficult.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Venezuelan Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Venezuelan is allowed to bowl along in front without any genuine pressure, dictating a measured pace throughout.
scenarios.body: If Venezuelan is allowed to bowl along in front without any genuine pressure, dictating a measured pace throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fill Gaps
scenarios.trigger: If Venezuelan fades in the final quarter-mile and Solar Pass or Shipshape, travelling smoothly just off the pace, inherit the lead.
scenarios.body: If Venezuelan fades in the final quarter-mile and Solar Pass or Shipshape, travelling smoothly just off the pace, inherit the lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and open a gap for hold-up horses, with Midnight Rumble or Curran finishing strongly.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and open a gap for hold-up horses, with Midnight Rumble or Curran finishing strongly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Venezuelan is baulked or loses the lead at a critical point and the race breaks up into a muddling tactical affair.
scenarios.body: If Venezuelan is baulked or loses the lead at a critical point and the race breaks up into a muddling tactical affair.

watchPoints.text: Venezuelan — if it secures the lead cleanly at the start, watch whether any runner attempts to press it in the first half-mile; unchallenged, it is the dominant pace shape for the race.

Shipshape — watch how close David Probert positions it behind the leader in the first few furlongs; if it gets trapped wide or loses its prominent berth on Chester's narrow track, its chance diminishes sharply.

Ruler Legend — 247 days off the track for Gary Hanmer (0/7 over 14 days) means it needs to settle and travel smoothly into the race; any sign of rustiness or being caught wide at a bend would end its chance early.

Solar Pass — Jason Watson is likely to look for a position directly behind Venezuelan; if Solar Pass is squeezed or blocked behind a wall of horses on the tight Chester turns, it cannot express its prominent style effectively.

Curran — watch whether Tom Eaves attempts to ride more prominently than the hold-up tag suggests; a patient hold-up ride at Chester 2m is the hardest tactical ride in the race and any ground lost early is unlikely to be recovered.

races.name: Schweppes Cherry Pepper Handicap

runners_data.name: L'Eagle Aid
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on good going and has four placed efforts from ten outings on similar ground, making this trip and surface squarely in his comfort zone; Sean Bowen provides an upgrade and Charlie Johnston's 14-day strike rate is solid, so this horse is positioned to press early and make a bold challenge.|
runners_data.comment: His connections landed this race last year, and L’Eagle Aid has solid course and distance form on a sound surface; returning after 50 days off, he ran to form here last time though the handicapper may have his measure, with our figures placing him fourth in the field.

runners_data.name: Taritino
runners_data.note: Arrived here in fine form — a win and a second in his last two starts, both on good ground at 12f and 14f — and Taylor Fisher rides for a yard that rarely targets Chester without purpose; three wins from six placings on similar going underlines suitability, and he is one of the likeliest to actually secure a prominent pitch.|
runners_data.comment: Landing a handicap by 4½ lengths at Salisbury last time off a mark 6lb below today’s, Taritino came through with authority and handles any ground at this trip; a weight rise was inevitable after a performance that emphatic, but he may still have more to offer.

runners_data.name: Oman
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with a patchy record on good going (no wins or places from four attempts) and a headgear flag, he has been dropping in trip lately and the step back to 12½f here does not automatically suit; Toby Moore claims 7lb which helps the handicapper, but his form profile makes him an unlikely prominent player despite his natural inclination.|
runners_data.comment: A 2¼-length winner at Goodwood off a 3lb lower mark two starts back, Oman returns in first-time cheekpieces having slipped below that level most recently; he handles this trip and going well and is in decent form overall, though 3lb higher than his winning mark today.

runners_data.name: Triple Force
runners_data.note: Has a strong record on good turf (four wins, ten places from 13 outings) and wears headgear, suggesting he needs to be held up to concentration; Craig Lidster's yard has drawn a blank over the past 14 days and the horse may not get his desired prominent position given the congestion in this field, diluting his chance.|
runners_data.comment: Third beaten 3 lengths off this exact mark at York last time, Triple Force is consistent on a sound surface and tends to make the running; first-time cheekpieces are added today, but he remains 4lb above his last winning mark, making the principals difficult to beat.

runners_data.name: Percy Jones
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer who is suited by patients tactics, David Egan gives him every chance of finding a late run, though Chester's tight circuit and short straight make it structurally hard for a true hold-up horse to deliver; three places at 14f on good ground give him a profile that would suit a stronger pace scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten a length off this mark last time, Percy Jones showed a marginal improvement on his recent form and handles any ground at this trip; first-time cheekpieces are added, though he needs to find considerably more after a difficult mid-season patch.

runners_data.name: Spartan Times
runners_data.note: In good form — a win at 16f and placed efforts at 14-17f — but this horse's natural style is prominent, and with the field already saturated by prominent types he is the one most likely to be pushed back into an unnatural midfield role; the STYLE_FIT flag is a genuine concern and his chance is tempered accordingly, though Jennie Candlish sends him here fresh and in form.|
runners_data.comment: Fifth beaten 8½ lengths on his latest flat outing, Spartan Times has shown better form over hurdles but comes back here with something to prove; he handles the trip on good going and is 2lb lower today, though our figures rate him well behind the field.

runners_data.name: Atheneum
runners_data.note: Has been off for 81 days, the longest layoff in the field, and Philip Kirby's 14-day numbers are modest; two placed efforts at 14f on good and soft suggest he stays the trip, but the fitness query after a long absence and a deep draw into Chester's bends make him vulnerable to being outpaced early in a competitive affair.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth beaten 11 lengths at Southwell last time out, Atheneum has been off the track for 81 days and now gets first-time cheekpieces; he handles this distance on good going and could bounce back closer to his best, but he sits at the foot of our figures and faces a tough task.

runners_data.name: Condotti
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's yard is in active form (8 from 34 over 14 days) but this four-year-old's form readings are uninspiring — no wins on good ground, only one place from four turf attempts at shorter trips, and he steps up to 1m4½f off a modest rating of 60; his hold-up style is genuine but the form and trip profile leave him needing significant improvement.|
runners_data.comment: Third beaten 2 lengths off this mark at Hamilton last time, Condotti showed a marginal upturn in form and now adds first-time cheekpieces here; the concern is that he may be best at shorter and could find today’s trip a stamina test.

runners_data.name: Relentless Hero
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in this field, a three-year-old from Andrew Balding's in-form yard (9/60 over 14 days) who won last time at 10f on soft — the step up to 12½f on good is a question mark, but his uncontested lead is a major tactical asset; Jason Watson can dictate every yard at Chester and the key question is whether he stays the extra distance.|
runners_data.comment: A half-length maiden success at Lingfield last time puts Relentless Hero in good heart for a handicap debut, and a mark of 72 looks fair for what appears a modest field; he handles most ground conditions and is trained by a top course handler, making him the one to beat.

races.paceDynamic: Relentless Hero is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him from the gate, Jason Watson can dictate terms at a measured, energy-conserving gallop around Chester's tight, turning circuit over 1m4½f. Behind him, L'Eagle Aid, Taritino, Triple Force, and Oman all want prominent positions, creating a congested battle for the four or five spots immediately off the leader — that scrimmage through the first bend and again at the 2-3 furlong pole is where traffic incidents are most likely to materialise. The field holds more prominent-style types than can all occupy that ground, and L'Eagle Aid and Taritino — both proven on good ground at this trip — are best placed to actually secure early proximity, while Triple Force and Oman are most likely to be squeezed back. A controlled, even pace set by one uncontested front-runner at Chester historically compresses the field and rewards horses racing prominently in behind, meaning the race shape firmly favours prominent trackers who can travel into contention rather than true hold-up horses making ground from the rear.

scenarios.title: Relentless Hero Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Relentless Hero leads without serious pressure and sets a steady, even tempo that suits closers off his pace.
scenarios.body: If Relentless Hero leads without serious pressure and sets a steady, even tempo that suits closers off his pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble, Stronger Stayer Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent runners jostle fiercely for position early, elevating the pace and burning off the front-runner.
scenarios.body: If the four prominent runners jostle fiercely for position early, elevating the pace and burning off the front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically in the home straight and a long gap opens for finishers from the rear.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses dramatically in the home straight and a long gap opens for finishers from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front-Runner Poaches
scenarios.trigger: If Relentless Hero is allowed to dictate at a falsely slow pace and quickens clear before rivals can respond.
scenarios.body: If Relentless Hero is allowed to dictate at a falsely slow pace and quickens clear before rivals can respond.

watchPoints.text: Relentless Hero — if Watson steals a soft lead through the first bend uncontested, he could open a gap that the prominent scrimmage behind never fully closes; monitor his sectionals from the start.

L'Eagle Aid, Taritino, Triple Force and Oman — four horses wanting the same prominent ground on a tight, turning course means at least one faces a troubled run around the 2-3f pole; watch for crowding and checked momentum entering the home straight.

Spartan Times — racing out of his natural prominent role and mapped to midfield, any hesitation at the start or slow positioning could leave him trapped on the rail at Chester with nowhere to go; his run should be discounted if he cannot find a forward position early.
Atheneum — 81 days off the track is the longest layoff in the field and Chester's bends can expose a horse lacking a recent racecourse gallop; watch how quickly he acclimatises once the gates open.

Percy Jones and Condotti — genuine hold-up horses whose finishing effort will depend entirely on whether the pace is strong enough to open ground late; if Relentless Hero controls a steady pace, neither may ever get competitive.
